DrWrinch Shiny app: implementation plan

Source: PLAN_SHINY.md

This document captures the implementation plan produced by a planning agent on 2026-05-19. The plan is referenced from HANDOFF.md. Read both before starting.

0. Grounding from the codebase

What’s actually there:

  • Four exported functions in R/bf_binomial.R, R/bf_urn.R, R/sens_binomial.R, R/sens_urn.R; one internal .find_omega_tipping() in R/utils.R.
  • DESCRIPTION declares Depends: R (>= 4.0.0), Imports: stats, BiasedUrn, Suggests: ggplot2, dplyr, knitr, rmarkdown, testthat (>= 3.0.0), DrBristol. Version is 0.0.0.9002, CRAN submission pending (cran-comments.md exists).
  • inst/ currently holds only CITATION. No inst/shiny/ yet.
  • tests/testthat/ has three substantive test files; testthat edition 3.
  • .Rbuildignore is minimal; nothing about shinyapps.io/rsconnect yet.
  • The vignette (vignettes/getting-started.Rmd) is the canonical narrative the UI should mirror: paper example is y_W = 7, y_R = 3; threshold default is 20; sens_urn(7, 3)$omega_star ~= 1.304; bf_urn(7, 3) = 39; bf_binomial(5, 5) = bf_urn(5, 5) = 1.
  • Coding standards (~/repos/ai_workflow/CLAUDE_CODING.md) require: tests-before-implementation, “why” comments at branch points, devtools::document() + devtools::check() before complete, one-file-per-coherent-unit (files ~< 300 lines), bump patch on new exports, pause for review after tests, after implementation, and at any unresolved design decision.

Constraints this places on the plan:

  1. The app is essentially a thin GUI over four pure functions. Do not over-engineer.
  2. CRAN cares about: examples that do not block (\dontrun{} for run_app()), inst/ size (Shiny apps with heavy CSS/JS bloat the tarball), and that every package in Suggests is used only after a requireNamespace() guard inside run_app().
  3. The four functions already do all the validation we need — the server’s job is to translate Shiny inputs into well-formed calls, catch the documented NA_real_ / Inf outcomes, and render them with prose a non-R user understands.

1. File-by-file scaffold

1a. New code in R/

R/run_app.R (new, ~40 lines) - Exports run_app(). - Signature: run_app(launch_browser = interactive(), ...). The ... is forwarded to shiny::runApp() so power users can pass port, host, display.mode, etc. - Body, in order: 1. requireNamespace("shiny", quietly = TRUE) — if missing, stop("Install 'shiny' to use run_app(): install.packages('shiny')", call. = FALSE). Repeat for bslib and the chosen plot library. Why at runtime, not as hard Imports: keeps CRAN tarball small and keeps R CMD check honest about what’s actually needed to use the core BF functions from the command line. 2. app_dir <- system.file("shiny", package = "DrWrinch"); if app_dir == "" stop with a helpful message (“did you install from source without inst/?”). 3. shiny::runApp(appDir = app_dir, launch.browser = launch_browser, ...). - Roxygen with @examples \dontrun{ run_app() } (blocks otherwise) and @export. - Cross-references: @seealso [bf_binomial()], [bf_urn()].

Do not add any module/server R files under R/. Keep everything under inst/shiny/ so the app dir is self-contained and can be deployed independently to shinyapps.io without dragging the rest of the package source.

1b. App under inst/shiny/

Use ui.R + server.R + global.R (rather than a single app.R) for three reasons: (i) shinyapps.io and rsconnect::deployApp() recognize either, (ii) global.R is the conventional place to put library calls and helper sourcing that needs to happen exactly once at app start, (iii) it makes the file-per-coherent-unit rule easier to honor without 600-line app.R.

inst/shiny/
  global.R              # library() calls, source() helpers, app constants
  ui.R                  # bslib page, single-screen layout
  server.R              # reactives, validation, rendering
  R/
    helpers.R           # pure functions: format_bf(), bf_label(), input checks
    plots.R             # omega-sensitivity curve, BF axis-of-evidence strip
  www/
    custom.css          # 20-40 lines of tweaks for the Jeffreys-scale strip
    NOTES.md            # one-paragraph "what this app shows" for shinyapps.io landing
  rsconnect/            # generated by rsconnect on first deploy; .gitignored

(deploy.R is NOT shipped in inst/; lives at repo root.)

Concrete contents:

inst/shiny/global.R (~20 lines) - library(shiny), library(bslib), library(DrWrinch), plot lib (see Decision A). - source("R/helpers.R", local = TRUE); source("R/plots.R", local = TRUE). (Shiny auto-sources files in an R/ subdir under the app dir as of Shiny 1.5; sourcing explicitly is belt-and-braces and clearer.) - App-level constants: JEFFREYS_BREAKS <- c(1, 3, 10, 30, 100), JEFFREYS_LABELS <- c("anecdotal", "moderate", "strong", "very strong", "decisive"), THRESHOLD_DEFAULT <- 20.

inst/shiny/ui.R (~100 lines) - bslib::page_sidebar() (or page_fillable + layout_sidebar); theme = bslib::bs_theme(bootstrap_version = 5, preset = "bootstrap") (match _pkgdown.yml’s Bootstrap 5). - Sidebar: input controls (see section 4). - Main: a bslib::navset_card_tab() with three tabs — “Result”, “Sensitivity”, “About”. The “About” tab embeds a short paragraph plus a bslib::card_body() with rendered HTML mirroring the vignette’s “when does each model apply?” table.

inst/shiny/server.R (~120 lines, hard cap before splitting into modules) - Standard function(input, output, session) signature. - Reactives in order: validated inputs -> bf results -> sensitivity results -> plot data. See section 5.

inst/shiny/R/helpers.R (~80 lines) - validate_counts(y_W, y_R): returns a shiny::validate(need(...)) chain. Why a separate function: same checks needed by both result and sensitivity render paths. - format_bf(bf): takes the numeric BF, returns a list of value (formatted string, e.g. “39.0” or “>10,000” or “undefined (RTF urn too small)”), verdict (Jeffreys label), direction (“favors working theory” / “favors rival” / “no evidence either way”). Handles NA_real_ and Inf explicitly. Why a single formatter: both models route their numerical outputs through the same UI prose, so non-R users see consistent language. - bf_label(bf): maps numeric BF to one of JEFFREYS_LABELS based on cut() against JEFFREYS_BREAKS (with the symmetric treatment of 1/bf for BFs < 1). - interpret_omega_star(om): e.g., returns “Pro-H1 items would have to be roughly 30% more likely to be observed than pro-rival items for the conclusion to fail at threshold 20.” Handles 0, NA, and finite cases.

inst/shiny/R/plots.R (~80 lines) - plot_bf_vs_omega(y_W, y_R, model = c("binomial", "urn"), threshold): computes BF over omegas <- exp(seq(log(0.25), log(8), length.out = 80)) (log-spaced because BF is decreasing and the action is near 1), draws horizontal line at threshold, vertical line at omega_star if defined. Why log-spaced: matches the monotone-decreasing structure of BF in omega and gives equal visual weight to omega < 1 (bias against H1) and omega > 1 (bias for H1). - plot_jeffreys_strip(bf): a simple discrete-color bar with markers — useful because the target audience is humanists, not statisticians. Optional for MVP. - plot_bf_vs_M(y_W, y_R, threshold, M_max = 50) for the binomial tab only: bar chart of BF at each rival-favoring pseudo-observation count.

1c. Adjustments to existing files

.Rbuildignore: append ^inst/shiny/rsconnect$, ^deploy\.R$, ^inst/shiny/www/NOTES\.md$, ^HANDOFF\.md$, ^PLAN_SHINY\.md$. - Why inst/shiny/rsconnect/ is rebuilt by rsconnect::deployApp() and contains a per-deploy hash; you do not want it in the package tarball.

DESCRIPTION: bump version to 0.0.1.9000 (new exported function run_app() per the coding-standards bump rule). Add to Suggests: - shiny, bslib, plot lib (see Decision A), and shinytest2 (testing, see section 6). - Do not promote any of these to Imports. The app is genuinely optional; CRAN reviewers prefer Suggests for runtime-only dependencies that gate behind requireNamespace().

NAMESPACE: regenerated by devtools::document(). Will add export(run_app).

NEWS.md: prepend a new # DrWrinch 0.0.1.9000 block: “Added run_app(), an interactive Shiny app for the two models and their sensitivity tipping points. Hosted at <shinyapps.io URL>.”

_pkgdown.yml: add a new reference section “Interactive app” with contents: run_app. Also consider adding articles: pointing to a future vignettes/articles/app-tour.Rmd (deferred; phase 4).

2. Design decisions you should make explicitly

These are real choices. Each has a recommendation and a trade-off.

Decision A — Plot library: ggplot2 vs. plotly. - Recommendation: ggplot2. It’s already in Suggests. The plots are small, static, and need to look right in a screenshot; plotly’s interactivity (hover, zoom) is a nice-to-have here, not a need-to- have. Adding plotly means another heavy dependency that bloats shinyapps.io image size and slows cold-start. - Trade-off: with ggplot2 you give up hover-tooltips on the omega curve. Mitigation: print the numeric omega_star with a clear annotation on the plot. If you later want interactivity, swap to plotly with one helper change.

Decision B — Tab vs. accordion vs. side-by-side for the two models. - Recommendation: side-by-side cards on a single screen, sharing one set of inputs. The whole point of the vignette is that you usually want both BFs reported together (“when in doubt, compute both”). Forcing the user to flip a tab to compare binomial-vs-urn defeats this. - Trade-off: on narrow screens this stacks; that is fine on bslib::layout_columns(col_widths = c(6,6)) which auto-collapses. - Alternative if you prefer: a radioButtons("model", ...) with one card. Do not do this — it hides the comparison.

Decision C — Should theta_cut and prior_a, prior_b be exposed? - Recommendation: hide theta_cut, prior_a, prior_b behind a collapsible “Advanced” bslib::accordion_panel. The target audience will not know what these are. Default to theta_cut = 0.5, prior_a = prior_b = 1. Power users open the accordion. - Trade-off: discoverability of the prior-sweep sensitivity feature. Mitigation: the “Sensitivity” tab text describes M_star (“M extra pseudo-observations favoring the rival”) in plain prose regardless of whether the prior accordion is open.

Decision D — Should the app support the urn model’s domain restriction gracefully? - Yes, mandatory. bf_urn(2, 10) returns NA_real_. The server must detect this and render a clear “the urn model is undefined here because the rival-favorable urn cannot supply a sample of size n = y_W + y_R when y_R > y_W + 1” message in the urn card, while still showing the binomial result. This is exactly the kind of friction that drives non-R users away if not handled.

Decision E — Single shinyapps.io account vs. team. - The plan author cannot decide this. If rsconnect::accounts() returns one for jwbowers already, deploy under that. Otherwise the user needs to register at https://shinyapps.io and run rsconnect::setAccountInfo(). Flag this at the deploy step.

Decision F — CRAN submission timing. - The plan author recommends submitting the current 0.0.0.9002 (four core functions, clean check) first, then adding run_app() in 0.0.1 afterward. Cleaner first submission; deploy script depends on the CRAN binary existing.

3. Dependencies (DESCRIPTION changes)

Add to Suggests (not Imports):

shiny (>= 1.7.0),
bslib (>= 0.6.0),
ggplot2,           # already in Suggests; no change needed
shinytest2,        # for snapshot tests
rsconnect          # only for the deploy.R helper

shinytest2 and rsconnect should be conditionally loaded in tests (testthat::skip_if_not_installed) and in deploy.R (requireNamespace guard).

Why not Imports for any of these: the only entry point from the rest of the package into the app is run_app(), which requireNamespace-guards every Shiny call. A user who installs DrWrinch just to compute Bayes factors should never need Shiny.

Why a version floor on shiny and bslib: bslib::page_sidebar() and bslib::navset_card_tab() need bslib >= 0.6. shiny::bindEvent()-style reactivity needs shiny >= 1.6. The floors are conservative.

Input controls and ranges:

Input id Control Default Valid range Notes
y_W numericInput step=1 min=0 7 non-neg integer coerce with as.integer server-side; warn on non-integer
y_R numericInput step=1 min=0 3 non-neg integer same
threshold numericInput step=1 min=1e-6 20 positive the 20 cutoff matches the vignette
theta_cut sliderInput step=0.05 0.5 (0, 1) exclusive hidden in accordion
prior_a, prior_b numericInput step=0.5 min=0.01 1, 1 positive hidden in accordion

Validation messages must be human-readable: “Enter a non-negative whole number for y_W”, not "need(is.numeric(input$y_W) && input$y_W >= 0)".

5. Server logic

Reactive graph (read top-down, dependencies flow downward):

inputs$y_W, inputs$y_R, inputs$threshold, ...
    |
    v
counts_ok  <- reactive({ validate(...); list(y_W = ..., y_R = ...) })
    |
    +---> bf_binom <- reactive({ bf_binomial(c$y_W, c$y_R, ...) })
    +---> bf_urn_v <- reactive({ bf_urn(c$y_W, c$y_R) })
    +---> sens_b   <- reactive({ sens_binomial(c$y_W, c$y_R, threshold) })
    +---> sens_u   <- reactive({ sens_urn(c$y_W, c$y_R, threshold) })
            |
            +---> output$result_binom (renderUI: card with formatted BF)
            +---> output$result_urn   (renderUI: card with formatted BF; NA-aware)
            +---> output$plot_omega   (renderPlot)
            +---> output$plot_M       (renderPlot)
            +---> output$tipping_text (renderUI: prose summary)

Key implementation choices:

  1. Wrap each model call in tryCatch — bf_binomial() uses stats::integrate() which can fail at pathological omega. Catch and render a friendly “computation failed at omega = X; try a narrower range” message rather than letting Shiny show a red error.
  2. Treat NA_real_ (urn undefined) and Inf (rival probability zero) as expected branches, not errors. The card renders prose explaining each.
  3. Debounce the omega-plot computation with shiny::debounce(200) — typing y_W = 1, 17, 170 should not recompute the 80-point omega sweep three times. The numeric BF outputs do not need debouncing (microseconds).
  4. No global state, no <<-, no reactiveValues unless required. Reactives + eventReactive if you add the Recompute button.
  5. Use req() early to short-circuit when inputs are NULL during initial render (Shiny renders before user input).

6. Testing strategy

Three layers, prioritized:

Layer 1 — Pure helpers (testthat, runs in CI, fast). File: tests/testthat/test-app_helpers.R. - format_bf(39) returns verdict = "strong", direction = "favors working theory". - format_bf(1) returns verdict = "no evidence", neutral direction. - format_bf(NA_real_) returns verdict = "undefined" with explanatory text. - format_bf(Inf) returns a high-evidence verdict, not a crash. - interpret_omega_star(0) returns the “fails at baseline” prose. - interpret_omega_star(NA_real_) returns the “robust to any bias” prose. - interpret_omega_star(1.304) returns a numeric percentage interpretation. - bf_label() maps boundaries (1, 3, 10, 30, 100) into the correct Jeffreys bin.

These tests must be written before the helpers are implemented (per coding standards).

How they access the helper code: at the top, source(system.file( "shiny/R/helpers.R", package = "DrWrinch")) after devtools::load_all(). Why — keeping helpers under inst/shiny/R/ and not under the package’s own R/ means they’re not part of the namespace; tests have to source them explicitly. The alternative is to move helpers into R/app_helpers.R and export them as @keywords internal, which is recommended only if a third test layer ends up needing them.

Layer 2 — Server logic (testthat + shiny::testServer). File: tests/testthat/test-app_server.R. skip_if_not_installed("shiny"). - Construct a testServer(app = "inst/shiny", expr = { ... }) block. - Set session$setInputs(y_W = 7, y_R = 3, threshold = 20) and assert bf_binom() ~= 7.83, bf_urn_v() == 39, sens_u()$omega_star ~= 1.304. - Set y_W = 2, y_R = 10 and assert bf_urn_v() is NA and the urn card output contains “undefined”. - Set y_W = 5, y_R = 5 and assert both BFs are 1.

These are substantive in the sense the coding standards require: they test the principle that the app correctly translates the paper’s claims into UI state, not just that it does not crash.

Layer 3 — Snapshot/visual (shinytest2, runs locally only). File: tests/testthat/test-app_snapshot.R. Top: skip_on_cran(), skip_on_ci() (or skip on CI unless you wire up a headless Chrome action), skip_if_not_installed("shinytest2"). - One snapshot of initial render at y_W = 7, y_R = 3. - One snapshot of the urn-undefined branch. - One snapshot of the sensitivity tab.

shinytest2 snapshots are large and fragile across OSes; keep these to a handful and skip on CRAN.

Update tests/testthat.R: no change needed, test_check("DrWrinch") already picks up new files.

7. Deployment to shinyapps.io

The constraint is one source of truth: the same inst/shiny/ dir runs locally via run_app() and gets deployed to shinyapps.io. That’s straightforward because rsconnect::deployApp(appDir = "inst/shiny") packages exactly that directory.

File: deploy.R at repo root (not under inst/, not shipped): - Top: if (!requireNamespace("rsconnect", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("rsconnect"). - Then: short comment about needing rsconnect::setAccountInfo(...) first time. - Body: r rsconnect::deployApp( appDir = "inst/shiny", appName = "drwrinch", appTitle = "DrWrinch: Bayes factors for process tracing", appFiles = c("global.R", "ui.R", "server.R", "R/helpers.R", "R/plots.R", "www/custom.css"), forceUpdate = TRUE ) - The explicit appFiles allowlist prevents accidental deployment of rsconnect/, NOTES.md, or any local .RData.

Critical: shinyapps.io does not have DrWrinch installed. The app must depend on the package as published. Two options:

Option 1 (recommended for the medium term): publish DrWrinch to CRAN first, then deploy. The library(DrWrinch) in global.R resolves cleanly against the CRAN binary. This is the cleanest path and aligns with the existing cran-comments.md.

Option 2 (for the demo before CRAN): use remotes::install_github() in a setup step. rsconnect does not run arbitrary setup, but it does honor the package manifest written by rsconnect::writeManifest(). The hack: add if (!requireNamespace("DrWrinch")) remotes::install_github("bowers- illinois-edu/DrWrinch") at the top of global.R. This works but slows cold-start by ~30s and is fragile to GitHub rate limits. Use only as a stopgap.

Recommendation: go with Option 1. It also gives you the CRAN release as a natural milestone.

.Rbuildignore additions (re-stating from 1c, with reasons): - ^deploy\.R$ — repo helper, not part of the package. - ^inst/shiny/rsconnect$ — generated per-deploy state. - ^inst/shiny/www/NOTES\.md$ — landing-page notes for shinyapps.io, not for the R package tarball.

8. CRAN-readiness

Specific things R CMD check is going to complain about if we are not careful:

  1. run_app() examples block. Wrap in \dontrun{} (not \donttest{} — even --run-donttest will time out). The roxygen example block is already drafted this way in section 1.
  2. inst/shiny/ size. Keep www/ to essentials: 1 small CSS file (~2KB). No fonts, no images, no bundled JS libraries. shinyapps.io will load Bootstrap from CDN via bslib.
  3. Suggests not actually optional? CRAN flags Suggests-listed packages that the package uses unconditionally. Verify: every library() in global.R and source() in helpers.R/plots.R is inside inst/, so R CMD check’s static analysis will not see them. The only package-side reference is requireNamespace() calls in R/run_app.R, which is correct.
  4. No visible binding for global variable notes from R CMD check on ggplot’s aesthetics. Mitigation: in plots.R, declare with utils::globalVariables(c("omega", "bf")) at the top of the file, or use aes(x = .data$omega, ...) with @importFrom rlang .data. Since helpers live under inst/, R CMD check will not actually scan them — but if you later move helpers into R/, this becomes load-bearing.
  5. Spell-check. Add “shinyapps”, “Jeffreys”, “bslib” to inst/WORDLIST if you run devtools::spell_check().

The package is at 0.0.0.9002 with cran-comments.md ready. Decision F: do you want to land the Shiny app before the first CRAN submission, or push CRAN out for it? Recommendation: submit to CRAN first at the current state (it’s clean, the four core functions are the contribution), then add run_app() in 0.0.1 as a follow-up release. This keeps the first CRAN submission simple and means the deploy-to-shinyapps story (which needs a CRAN binary) works on day one of the app’s release.

9. Phased implementation order

Phase 0 — Plan approval (this document). Resolve decisions A–F above before writing any code.

Phase 1 — MVP scaffolding (1–2 hours). 1. Write tests/testthat/test-app_helpers.R first (Layer 1). All tests should fail or skip cleanly. 2. Checkpoint: pause for user review of tests. 3. Implement R/run_app.R with requireNamespace guards and \dontrun{} example. 4. Implement inst/shiny/global.R, ui.R, server.R with the side-by-side card layout, no plots, no sensitivity tab — just the two BFs and the Jeffreys verdict. 5. Implement inst/shiny/R/helpers.R to satisfy Layer 1 tests. 6. Bump DESCRIPTION to 0.0.1.9000, add Suggests, update NAMESPACE via devtools::document(). 7. devtools::check(). Resolve notes. 8. Checkpoint: pause for user review of MVP. User runs devtools::load_all(); run_app() locally.

Phase 2 — Sensitivity tab and plots. 1. Write tests/testthat/test-app_server.R (Layer 2) — pass y_W=7,y_R=3,threshold=20, expect sens_u()$omega_star ~= 1.304. 2. Checkpoint: review tests. 3. Implement inst/shiny/R/plots.R and wire the sensitivity tab in ui.R/server.R. 4. Checkpoint: review look-and-feel. Decision A (plotly vs ggplot) is final here.

Phase 3 — Polish and resilience. 1. NA / Inf branch handling in helpers and server. 2. Friendly validation messages. 3. About tab with vignette-style prose. 4. inst/shiny/www/custom.css — minor color/spacing tweaks. 5. tests/testthat/test-app_snapshot.R (Layer 3) — opt-in, local only. 6. Checkpoint: full devtools::check() pass; pause for review.

Phase 4 — Deployment. 1. (Assuming Decision F = “CRAN first”) publish CRAN release of 0.0.1. 2. Create deploy.R at repo root. 3. First-time rsconnect::setAccountInfo() by the user (requires shinyapps.io credentials). 4. source("deploy.R"); verify the live URL. 5. Update README.md with the live URL; mention in NEWS.md. 6. Checkpoint: end-to-end review. User hits the live URL on a tablet.

Phase 5 (optional) — Polish for paper release. 1. vignettes/articles/app-tour.Rmd — pkgdown-only article (not a CRAN vignette) with screenshots. 2. Add the live URL to inst/CITATION notes. 3. Open-graph metadata in inst/shiny/www/ for nice social-media link previews.

Each checkpoint is a literal stop-and-wait for the user, per their coding-standards file.

10. Risks and things to flag now

  1. shinyapps.io free tier limits. 5 active hours/month and concurrency caps. For a paper-demo audience this is usually fine but is worth noting if the paper goes viral. The deploy script can be re-pointed to Posit Connect Cloud or RStudio Connect later with one URL change.
  2. BiasedUrn::dFNCHypergeo on shinyapps.io. This is on CRAN, so it will install cleanly. No risk.
  3. Cold start time. shinyapps.io spins down idle apps after ~5 min. First hit after sleep takes 10–20s. Mitigation: a small “scheduled keep-warm” GitHub Action that curls the URL every 4 minutes during business hours. Out of scope for MVP.
  4. Mobile usability. Process-tracing scholars at conferences may pull this up on phones. bslib::page_sidebar() collapses the sidebar to a drawer on small screens by default; verify on a phone before finalizing.
  5. Reproducibility of omega_star. The vignette claims ~= 1.3 for (7, 3). The Shiny app must show numbers that exactly match the package, since the vignette and the app share a citation. The server should call sens_urn() directly rather than recomputing the search itself.
